transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-04-11
- Start: 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood Product), Dr. Priya Rao (Elysian Head of ML), Elliot Shaw (VP Eng), Samir Patel (Data Eng), Ava Morgan (Security), Jordan Lee (PM)
- Recording: link omitted

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): quick demo of JSON output contracts, showed failures and tool-call integration, flagged network/audit questions.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. Quick round of intros if we need them but I think we have most of the team on the call.
[00:12] Dr. Priya Rao: Hi all, Priya here. We're particularly interested in structured response enforcement for clinical extraction tasks and ensuring we don't leak PHI.
[00:20] Elliot Shaw: Elliot, VP Eng — want a solution that has predictable latency and doesn't blow our cost projections.
[00:26] Samir Patel: Samir — we'll provide sample payloads today after the call.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Great. Today's agenda: 1) Console walkthrough of the Output Contract editor, 2) Live API demo of JSON mode with function calling + guarded fallbacks, 3) Cost/perf suggestions via Optimize, and 4) Q&A and next steps.
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: I'll drive the demo; I'll start in the Console then flip to the API and show a small benchmark.

[02:10] [Liam O'Connor shares screen] All right I'm in the Console. On the left is the model route; I've selected rdl-medium-03 as example. Under 'Output Contracts' you can see a schema editor, we support json-schema-ish syntax and also a simplified contract DSL.
[02:28] Jordan Lee: Quick question — can we pin multiple versions of the contract and rollout? We have a dev/stage/prod flow.
[02:34] Sofia Alvarez: Yes — each route has versioned contracts, and you can canary a contract change to a subset of traffic or to a dedicated tag.
[03:00] [00:03:20] Dr. Priya Rao: When enforcement is on, what happens to outputs that don't validate? We need to surface failures into our logs and never accept a malformed record into downstream ETL.
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: Good question. We have three modes: warn, fail, and transform. 'Fail' returns an error to the caller and increments a contract failure metric that writes to audit logs. 'Warn' returns the result but emits an event. 'Transform' will attempt a safe correction path via a secondary model or deterministic rule.
[03:35] Ava Morgan: On the logs and audit piece, we need tamper-evidence and integration with our KMS/HSM. Does Redwood store full responses? What's retention?
[03:43] Liam O'Connor: By default hosted retains short-term traces for debugging; for Private/Dedicated you control retention and we support sending audit streams to your SIEM. We integrate with KMS for encrypting keys and provide signed audit logs for compliance use-cases.

[05:00] [05:10] Liam O'Connor: Switching to a live example now. I'm going to define a contract for 'clinical_extraction' with fields: patient_id (string), encounter_date (date), problem_list (array of codes), severity (enum: mild, moderate, severe), notes (string max 2000). I'm going to attach a post-processing function 'anonymize_patient' as a tool call if PHI is detected.
[05:30] [05:31] Maya Chen: Note: the function call is executed server-side inside the Redwood runtime — you can choose to allow only verified functions to run.
[06:00] [06:05] Liam O'Connor: Hitting the Console 'Test' button with a sample clinical note. Expecting a JSON payload back. 
[06:18] [06:20] Transcript engine: returned result... parser did a partial parse... see there's a small malformed date string here.
[06:30] Dr. Priya Rao: Okay I can see why the date got messy — different providers use different date formats. Can we normalize?
[06:35] Liam O'Connor: That's where the 'transform' mode helps. You can configure normalization rules — we shipped a date-normalizer plugin that tries iso8601 coercion and falls back to heuristics, and then the contract validator re-checks.
transcript_continued:
[08:00] [Liam O'Connor] Now I'll flip to the API. Curl example up: POST /v1/generate with mode=json, contract_id=clinical_extraction_v2, function_call=anonymize_patient. Watch the headers: we set x-redwood-route, authorization, and we pass 'strict: true' in the body to enforce fail-on-invalid.
[08:20] [Samir Patel] Quick latency question — what's the overhead of strict JSON mode?
[08:25] [Liam O'Connor] Good call — typically on our rdl-medium-03 we've seen ~5-12ms added for contract validation on top of generation for small payloads; for longer sequences that overhead becomes negligible relative to generation time.
[09:10] [Maya Chen] For Dedicated we can keep that lower by colocating the validator and using warmed kernels.
[10:00] [Elliot Shaw] Cost perspective — does the transform mode multiply token usage because of a secondary model call?
[10:10] [Liam O'Connor] If transform uses a secondary model you will incur additional tokens; Optimize can profile expected token delta and recommend either a lighter transformer or a deterministic rule to avoid extra model calls.
[12:00] [12:12] [Demo glitch] the function-call returned a 502 because the post-processing function timed out — that's a config we can tune.
[12:35] [Sofia Alvarez] In the Console you can set timeouts per function and automatic fallbacks to 'warn' or 'fail' paths. We also expose a 'circuit breaker' to avoid cascading latencies.
[14:05] [14:10] [Liam] I'll run a small batch of 50 notes to show how batching and KV cache impact throughput; starting now.
[15:00] [Transcript engine] partial transcriptions... we can see batching improved throughput ~3.8x for common prefix lengths. There was some noise in the transcript where 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'kay vee cash' earlier.
[16:30] Dr. Priya Rao: About PHI — can we prevent even metadata leaks? For instance, if a model suggests private provider names accidentally.
[16:45] Liam O'Connor: We recommend a multi-layer approach: 1) prompt engineering + redaction rules onboarded in the Input Sanitizer, 2) contract enforcement to block disallowed fields, 3) optional post-hoc anonymization tool calls that replace detected PII, and 4) network-level egress rules in Private deployments.
[18:20] Ava Morgan: For KMS — do you integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS? We have a hybrid cloud setup.
[18:30] Liam O'Connor: Yes, key wrapping via AWS KMS and GCP KMS is supported; HSM integrations for Private are available too. We'll share the security deck.
[20:00] [20:05] Liam O'Connor: Now jumping to Optimize suggestions. For this EHR extraction workload, token distribution is: small prompt, long-ish notes, short structured output. Optimize suggests: rdl-medium-03 with 8-bit quantization for post-proc, enable KV cache for repeated patient prefixes, and a batching window of 40ms with a max batch of 16 for best latency/cost tradeoff.
[21:15] Elliot Shaw: Can Optimize surface expected cost delta for different quantization options?
[21:25] Sofia Alvarez: Exactly — Optimize shows estimated tokens, token cost, inferred accuracy delta from our evals, and a recommended profile you can apply directly to the route.
[22:00] [22:05] Samir Patel: We need to measure end-to-end P50/P95 with the function call and the anonymizer — do you have a script?
[22:12] Liam O'Connor: I will attach a benchmark script to the follow-up; it runs parallel clients and captures contract failure rates and latencies.
[24:00] [24:10] Maya Chen: Let's try a scenario: ask the model to output an array of problem codes but include a deliberate extra field — watch the contract enforcement.
[24:25] [Demo] the response returns success but contract flagged 'unexpected_field' and because route is set to 'fail' it returned HTTP 422 with a payload describing the mismatch.
[25:00] Dr. Priya Rao: That's useful — we want clear error codes for our ingestion pipeline.
[25:05] Liam O'Connor: Error codes are structured too; we include machine-friendly reasons and human messages.
[27:00] [27:10] Ava Morgan: On private deployments — we need a network diagram for firewall rules and egress. Also SLA for retention of audit logs.
[27:20] Maya Chen: We'll include a sample network diagram and the Dedicated/Private SLA terms in the follow-up.
[29:00] [29:05] [Participant - Jordan] Is there any way to have inline contract hints for the model, so it's guided towards the right types rather than just failing downstream?
[29:12] Liam O'Connor: Yes — we inject soft schema hints into the prompt in 'assist' mode. It nudges the model to prefer the right shape without hard failing. You can choose strictness per route.
[31:00] [31:05] [Demo] show of function-call flow: model suggests calling anonymize_patient with detected PHI, runtime validates function signature against allowed tools and executes the function with sanitized context.
[32:30] [32:40] Samir Patel: Any way to run the anonymizer deterministically so results are reproducible across runs?
[32:45] Liam O'Connor: Deterministic transforms are available if you use rule-based or deterministic libraries; ML-based anonymizers are probabilistic but we provide audit diffs and a delta scorer to review changes.
[34:20] [34:30] [Transcript noise] little stutter... Liam: sorry — lost the share for a sec.
[35:10] [35:15] [Maya Chen] Quick pricing note — pilot pricing is typically a capped monthly commit with a consumption overlay; we'll send exact numbers but expect engineering pilot rates are favorable for evaluation.
[36:45] Elliott Shaw: We will need to get legal involved for a data processing addendum if we go private.
[37:00] Ava Morgan: Also need to confirm SOC2 + penetration test cadence.
[37:10] Sofia Alvarez: We have SOC2 Type II reports and a penetration test summary; we'll include the artifacts and coordinate an NDA if needed for full reports.
[38:50] [38:55] [Open question] Dr. Priya Rao: If a contract change is rolled out and increases failure rate significantly, can we auto-rollback?
[39:05] Liam O'Connor: Yes — our rollout engine supports automated rollback thresholds tied to contract failure metrics and traffic tags.
[40:20] [40:30] [Wrap up] Maya Chen: Recap — Redwood to send pricing, security deck, network diagram, benchmark script. Elysian to send sample payloads and confirm pilot team and timeline. Pilot kickoff proposed for week of Apr 21.
[41:05] [Closing] Elliot: Thanks — good demo. We'll review docs and get back with dates.
[41:15] [End recording]
